mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime, or the rate stays below 4% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which raises perceived risk and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in one month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the 20-day forward return is not negatively correlated with the combined signal (Pearson IC > 0.3 or p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST and GDPC1) predicts a near-term expansion in economic activity, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >5% while HOUST and GDPC1 both increase by >3% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) when the combined signal is present in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the goods price index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates easing supply constraints, which lowers production costs and supports higher corporate earnings forecasts, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the observed INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month while the Federal Funds rate remains steady, it suggests inflationary pressure that discourages long-term equity investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in a month with no concurrent change in FEDFUNDS
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the 60-day forward return is not negatively correlated with the CPIAUCSL surprise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies but inferred from labor market momentum) combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates softening labor demand, which raises risk aversion and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.3 percentage points over two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly negative when UNRATE is rising (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer demand (HOUST) and business demand (GDPC1) above their 12-month averages for two months predicts a robust economic recovery that supports optimism in corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month average AND GDPC1 > 12-month average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return (p > 0.05) when both proxies are above trend in the regime.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three months suggests successful supply-side constraints, lowering growth fears and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in a moderate growth regime.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no outperformance versus a 2% CPIAUCSL baseline in the specified regime.
